description:
FILED s529a (Opus agent, 2026-10-31) while fixing #3824.  PRE-EXISTING for the variable-copy spelling; the element spellings were right on main only BY the #3824 alias.

A re-bless of an ARRAY / CODE (non-hash) referent through ONE copy of the reference is not seen through another copy.  perl blesses the REFERENT, so every reference to it sees the new class.

REPRO (scratch/s529a/pr/b1.pl rows 11 21 22 24):
    my $o3 = bless [], 'K'; my @c = ($o3); bless $o3, 'Other'; print ref($c[0]), "\n";   # perl Other
    my $od = bless [], 'K'; my $re = $od; bless $od, 'Other'; print ref($re), "\n";       # perl Other
    my $oe = bless [], 'K'; my @ce = ($oe); bless $ce[0], 'Other'; print ref($oe), "\n";  # perl Other
    my $og = bless [], 'K'; my %hg = (a => $og); bless $og, 'O2'; print ref($hg{a}), "\n"; # perl O2
  PCL (after #3824): K / K / K / K.  A HASH referent is right in every spelling (its class is the
  :__class__ key of the table itself).

MECHANISM: p-bless's array/code arm writes the class on the BOX it was handed (the variable or a
copy), and box-set / %p-container-snapshot copy that slot into every new container -- the slot is
both the cache and, for a raw vector / function payload, the ONLY record (ir-spec §2.6 "Array/code/glob
refs keep the class on the wrapper box").  Before #3824 the array construction arm stored the
VARIABLE's box itself, so rows 11 and 22 were right by aliasing (and `$c[0] = 3` rewrote $o3).

SHAPE TO MEASURE: a weak eq table referent -> class for vector / function payloads (the
*p-handle-stash* / *p-sv-stash* precedent: a count test keeps it off the hot path), written by
p-bless, read FIRST by %p-target-class; every reader that reads (p-box-class obj) directly as a
fast "is this an object" check must be audited (method dispatch, overload lookup) -- they would read
the stale cache.  Measure first how many direct slot readers there are.


=== AUDIT (s530a, 2026-10-31) -- every reader of the box class slot (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp + cl/pcl-xs.lisp, 55 sites) ===
CLASS ANSWER readers (they decide what ref / blessed / dispatch / "" print): %p-target-class (its wrapper arm read the wrapper's slot), p-get-class (slot fallback after %p-target-class), p-ref (slot fallback; raw ARRAY / CODE arms answered the reftype), box-sv (slot fallback after %p-target-class), p-overload-strval (via p-get-class), %p-builtin-blessed (via p-ref), %p-invocant-class (via p-get-class), pcl-xs.lisp:566 (via p-ref; slot only for a plain-valued referent box).  All reach the referent first through %p-target-class / p-get-class / p-ref, so ONE accessor serves them.
CACHE CARRIERS (copy the slot into a new box): box-set, %p-make-hash-entry, %p-container-snapshot, %p-assign-snapshot, %p-incdec-old, p-copy-scalar-arg, %p-tie-elem-value, pcl-xs.lisp:491, p-bless itself.
IS-OBJECT DISCRIMINATORS (keep a box vs unbox / plain fast arm): %p-append-box, %p-array-append, %p-hash-append, %p-elem-append, %p-concat-assign-value, p-.= (two), %p-operand-snapshot, %p-param-copy, %p-array-store-scalar, %p-hash-unbox-elem, %p-leavesub-scalar, %p-map-copy-scalar, %p-plain-scalar, %p-read-operand, p-return-value, %p-storable-raw, p-die, p-sprintf, %p-tie-elem-box, p-warn-is-reference.  A stale slot still says "object" (a referent never becomes unblessed), so these need no change for a RE-bless.  Residue: %p-compound-x-slow's `$obj OP= x` overload guard reads the slot -- it is right for a re-bless (non-nil either way); the nil-slot case belongs to #4061.

=== DONE (s530a) ===
FIX (cl/ only, emission IDENTICAL): a RE-bless of an ARRAY / CODE referent into a DIFFERENT class (through any box whose cached class already named one, or of a referent re-blessed before) is recorded ON THE REFERENT -- the weak table *p-rebless-stash* keyed by the vector / function, written by %p-note-rebless from both p-bless arms, read FIRST by %p-target-class (wrapper and raw arms through %p-held-referent-class), p-get-class and p-ref's raw arms through ONE accessor %p-rebless-class.  The read costs one fixnum test (sb-ext:defglobal *p-reblessed*) until a program re-blesses one.  Filehandles / globs keep *p-handle-stash* unchanged.
FIRST DESIGN MEASURED AND REPLACED: keying EVERY bless (the task's "class keyed by referent") passes the first-bless-after-copy rows too, but a weak SBCL gethash is ~54 ns vs ~3 ns strong and it sat on every method call / ref(): methret-arr +69 %, refarr 5x (scratch/s530a/bench4000.log).  That half is FILED as #4061 with the numbers and three candidate designs.
PROBES: scratch/s530a/pr/b1a.pl (13 rows) + b2a.pl (7 rows: dispatch, isa/can, overload "" through a re-blessed copy, a code object, local $_, filehandle / gensym stashes unchanged) identical to perl 5.40.3; the (b) rows of b1/b2/b6 are #4061.
GUARD: Pl/t/blessed-copy-01.t rows 5-6, inverse-verified (fail on 0fb05a79).
ir-spec §2.6: normative sentence "a re-bless of an ARRAY or CODE referent belongs to the referent" + the #4061 limit.
subject: a re-bless of an ARRAY / CODE referent through one copy of the reference is not seen through another (the class of a non-hash referent lives on each container)
